answer.rationale: With the contract lapsing in 14 days and the line at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, switching primary vendors (memory_c2) now carries unacceptable delivery risk despite its cost appeal, and renegotiating short-term price (memory_c4) has already been refused this cycle. The most promising path to meet the 18% cost mandate without disrupting supply is renewing the incumbent under a longer-term commitment, since memory_c6 indicates multi-year terms previously unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope. I want to verify memory_c6's archived source before committing, because the entire rationale for choosing renewal-with-restructured-terms over a risky vendor switch hinges on whether that volume-pricing benefit was robust and not confounded by other factors (e.g., a different component class or one-time rebate). If verification shows the multi-year discount was material and durable, renew_incumbent on a multi-year structure is the least-risk path to the cost target; if it was marginal or conditional, the decision may need to shift toward add_second_source or a guarded switch next cycle. This is flagged as a downstream value risk because committing to a multi-year term now could lock in suboptimal pricing if the 18% target isn't actually met, and because deferring is not viable given the hard 14-day expiration on a non-buffered line.
